newsitem.title: UK: Nat.Grid rejects OFFER price proposals.
newsitem.headline: Nat.Grid rejects OFFER price proposals.

text.p: National Grid Group Plc said proposals for the review of electricity transmission price controls proposed by power industry regulator OFFER in its fourth consultation paper were totally unacceptable and required significant changes if they were to be accepted.
National Grid, which runs the power transmission network in England and Wales, said proposals from OFFER were "too harsh, inconsistent and based on ill-founded assumptions."
National Grid said they would destabilise the balance between benefits for customers and returns for shareholders.
Chief executive David Jones said OFFER must make significant changes to make its proposals acceptable.
OFFER's plans included an effective revenue reduction of 22-28 percent for National Grid in 1997/98 and subsequent annual reductions of RPI minus 4.0 points.
National Grid said this would be excessive and lead to significant real price rises by 2001/02.
